Header: 2026-03-31 10:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (AtlasSearch ML Lead), Diego Ramos (Infra), Priya Nair (CTO)

Summary: Quick weekly sync to review latest quantization experiments (INT8 and FP8 variants), discuss quality regressions on the customer eval set, and agree next tuned runs and deliverables. Some noisy audio; auto-transcript has a few mis-terms (K V cache vs KV, Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated).

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 50 minutes today. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya: Maya here.
[00:08] Diego: Diego.
[00:10] Priya: Priya on.
[00:12] Jordan: Jordan and Sofia from our side. High level agenda: share the INT8/FP8 perf slides, go through the quality diffs on the eval set, then decide on tuning runs and action items.
[00:28] Sofia: I'll jump in on the perf numbers first. We ran three configs: FP16 baseline, INT8 post-training quant (per-channel), and an experimental FP8 path. All runs used the same sequence distribution from your prod traces Maya, about 75% short prompts (<128 tokens), 25% longer.
[00:45] Sofia: Summary numbers: INT8 gives roughly 1.7x throughput and ~1.8x token latency improvement at p50 compared to FP16 baseline on the same GPU instance; FP8 gives ~1.3x throughput and about 1.4x latency improvement. Those are median-ish; p95/p99 improvements are smaller when KV cache misses occur.
[01:12] Maya: Okay that's promising, can you share p95s? We care about tail latency for user-facing completions.
[01:17] Sofia: Yeah, p95 for FP16 is ~420ms, INT8 p95 sits at ~360ms, FP8 p95 ~380ms in our test environment. p99s were noisy due to batching artifacts but ballpark FP16 ~780ms, INT8 ~680ms, FP8 ~710ms. There's some variance tied to the KV cache hit rate.
[01:42] Diego: Are these numbers on Dedicated or hosted infra? We need to compare apples to apples with our on-prem nodes.
[01:47] Jordan: These are on a Redwood Dedicated pool using A100 gen2-ish hardware (we noted it as A100v2 in the sheet). We also ran a smaller Nvidia 4090-ish single-socket run for cost comparison but the main bench is Dedicated.
[02:05] Priya: About quality — what metric did you run against our eval set? We care about hallucinations and instruction-following accuracy not just BLEU.
[02:13] Sofia: Good call. We ran three automated slices: rouge-like similarity, a small instruction accuracy classifier, and a hallucination heuristic (based on ground-truth facts). On the aggregated eval set, INT8 shows a tiny delta: degradation around 0.6-0.9% relative on the instruction accuracy metric, FP8 a bit higher at ~1.2-1.8% depending on the prompt type.
[02:40] Maya: Hmm 1.8% on some prompt types could be noticeable. Which prompts are most impacted?
[02:45] Sofia: Long-form retrieval-heavy prompts and multi-step reasoning saw the largest deltas. Short chit-chat or templated completions were near identical. There's also some failure modes on numeric precision when tables or precise hashes are required.
[03:04] Diego: That aligns with our internal testing. The KV cache interplay matters — if cache is disabled or you get more misses, quantized models lose more quality.
[03:12] Sofia: Exactly, we've seen INT8 + KV cache enabled preserves much of the quality. In the runs where we force KV cache on prefixes (prefix caching), the instruction accuracy drop moves from ~0.9% to ~0.3% for INT8. FP8 improved similarly but still slightly worse than INT8 in some cases.
[03:30] Maya: Do we have an easy knob to toggle KV caching in your runtime?
[03:35] Jordan: Yes, in Redwood runtime it's a per-route config. We can enable prefix/KV caching per customer route; it also impacts cost and memory usage. We'll show the config snippet in the spreadsheet.
[03:46] Priya: Memory usage — how much more memory for caching with INT8 vs FP16?
[03:50] Sofia: INT8 is smaller model size, so KV cache is proportionally smaller in bytes too. However, enabling cache increases RAM usage for per-request state. On our Dedicated runs cache for the 1B-ish param model used about 12% extra GPU memory vs cache disabled; absolute sizes are in the bench sheet.
[04:08] Maya: Can you paste the link in chat? I didn't get the drive link yet.
[04:10] Jordan: Yep will drop it in a sec — link is in the notes: drive.google.com/open?id=redwood-quant-bench-2026 (auto-transcript often munges that).
[04:22] Sofia: Back to perf tradeoffs — batching helps throughput but hurts latency. For AtlasSearch's profile where 75% are short interactive prompts, we recommended small batching windows (5-10ms) plus prefix caching. That recovers much of INT8's throughput benefits while keeping p95 acceptable.
[04:45] Diego: We need p99 under 900ms for our interactive UI. Sounds borderline from your numbers.
[04:52] Sofia: In our worst-case bench p99 was ~680ms for INT8 which fits, but that's with cache and tuned batching. Without cache or with burst long sequences it can spike.
[05:04] Maya: On the quality side, can we look at a couple of failure examples?
[05:08] Sofia: Sure, I pulled two short examples. Example A: prompt asking for step-by-step config diff — FP16 gives correct ordered steps, INT8 missed a step; FP8 repeated a line. Example B: table numeric rounding — FP16 exact, INT8 had rounding differences in 2 of 10 cases. I'll paste them after the call.
[05:30] Maya: That would help. If it's only a small slice then we might accept INT8 for cheaper routes and keep FP16 for critical paths.
[05:38] Priya: Pricing — how much cost saving are we looking at if we go INT8 across the board?
[05:43] Jordan: Rough numbers: INT8 reduces token compute cost by ~35-40% compared to FP16; FP8 about 20-25%. Those are conservative and depend on batching and cache hit rates. Also Dedicated reserved pricing changes the economics more.
[05:58] Diego: We need an estimate for our monthly 99th percentile QPS peaks. We'll send you target QPS and sequence mix.
[06:06] Maya: Quick question: is INT8 a post-training quant only or did you try QAT (quant-aware training)?
[06:12] Sofia: These runs were post-training quant (PTQ) with the per-channel approach. We tried a small QAT pipeline as an experiment, which reduced some of the instruction accuracy deltas on the long-form slice but required a retrain pass and dataset from you. Tradeoff is time and infra.
[06:30] Maya: We don't have capacity to retrain right now, prefer PTQ.
[06:34] Sofia: Understood. PTQ + prefix KV cache + small-batch tuning seems like the recommended path.
[06:40] Jordan: Any security/compliance concerns on your side about model quantization or Dedicated runs?
[06:46] Priya: For us nothing specific to quantization, but we need audit logs for inference and keys in our KMS. If you could confirm logs are preserved in Private or Dedicated, that's helpful.
[06:57] Jordan: Yes, Redwood provides audit logs and KMS integrations for Private/Dedicated; we'll attach the SOC2/security doc and a brief on retention.
[07:06] Maya: Can you also confirm whether quantized weights are stored encrypted at rest in the Dedicated pool?
[07:12] Sofia: Yes, model artifacts in Dedicated are encrypted; on Private deployments that's customer-managed KMS. We'll add a short note.
[07:20] Diego: Back to bench — how did you measure hallucination heuristic? That method matters for us.
[07:25] Sofia: We used a simple entity/link-check: when the model asserts a fact present in the reference it counts as correct; if it invents an unsupported fact it's flagged. It's a heuristic, not perfect, but useful for relative comparisons. We'll provide the script and raw logs.
[07:40] Jordan: Okay next we should define the tuned runs we want: 1) INT8 with prefix KV cache enabled + small batching window (5ms), 2) INT8 with KV disabled to see worst-case tail behavior, 3) FP8 with cache on, 4) FP16 baseline with our suggested batching for cost baseline. Sofia, can you run those?
[08:00] Sofia: Yep, I'll kick off runs today — they take a few hours each. I'll also capture p50/p95/p99, quality metrics per prompt slice, and raw transcripts for the failure cases.
[08:10] Maya: We'd like you to run the INT8 + cache config on a node that mimics our on-prem 4x4090 cluster too if possible.
[08:18] Sofia: We have a 4090-like bench; we'll include that. Might have slightly different kernel perf but we'll annotate.
[08:26] Priya: For the final pilot we also care about autoscaling behavior and cold-starts — does quantization change cold-start spin-up time?
[08:34] Sofia: Good question — quantized models are smaller so checkpoint load time can be faster, but kernel compilation/caching sometimes adds overhead on first warm-up. In practice we saw similar cold-start within 10-20% faster for INT8 once kernels were available.
[08:50] Diego: Any gotchas for model variants? For example, if we have instruction- tuned vs base variants, does quantization behave differently?
[08:58] Sofia: Yes, instruction-tuned heads can be more sensitive if they rely on fine-param differences. It's model dependent; we'll add a note per variant.
[09:06] Maya: Timeline — how long until we have the tuned run results?
[09:09] Jordan: Sofia estimated by 2026-04-05 we should have all tuned runs + a slide with recommended route configs.
[09:16] Maya: Great. After that we'll review and decide which routes to flip to INT8.
[09:20] Priya: One more ops question: if we flip traffic to INT8 and see a regression in production, can Redwood route traffic back automatically?
[09:28] Jordan: Yes, we support canary rollouts and automatic rollback policies. We can configure per-route rollbacks on quality regressions if you provide the eval hooks.
[09:37] Sofia: Also we can expose a metric hook that pings your classifier and triggers alerts if instruction accuracy drops below threshold.
[09:43] Maya: Perfect.
[09:45] Jordan: Ok let's recap action items and owners...
[09:48] Jordan: Jordan will share the bench spreadsheet and raw eval logs (drive link) by 2026-04-02. Sofia will run the 4 tuned configs and post p50/p95/p99 + quality slices by 2026-04-05. Maya will send two additional production prompt sets and SLOs by 2026-04-03. Diego will confirm on-prem infra constraints by 2026-04-06. We'll schedule final pilot review week of 2026-04-13.
[10:12] Maya: Sounds good, thanks.
[10:14] Priya: Thanks all.
[10:16] Diego: Thanks.
[10:18] Jordan: I'll drop the notes and link after the call.
[10:21] End of recording.

Notes: The auto-transcript had occasional mis-terms: 'Redwood Dedicate' instead of 'Dedicated', 'K V cache' split, some names mispelled. We preserved those in parts to keep realism. The bench link and sheet will be attached as follow-up.
